sharp_disagreements.gist: Positive mutual information is the correct necessary condition; likelihood ratio measures amount.

sharp_disagreements.title: What Is Evidence?
sharp_disagreements.quote: a belief is only really worthwhile if you could, in principle, be persuaded to believe otherwise
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Principle as stated disqualifies arithmetic and itself; defends only empirical revisability.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Target is beliefs held regardless of evidence; mathematicians revise proofs; 2+2=3 essay covers arithmetic.

sharp_disagreements.title: What Is Evidence?
sharp_disagreements.quote: Therefore rational beliefs are contagious, among honest folk who believe each other to be honest.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Honest belief contagion is the recipe for information cascades converging on error.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Cascades arise from observing actions not evidence and are fragile; they are contagion without information.

sharp_disagreements.title: What Is Evidence?
sharp_disagreements.quote: that you believe for private reasons which are not transmissible
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Tacit expert knowledge is entangled but non-transmissible; essay can't separate it from floating belief.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Sapphire knowledge was transmitted by visit; tacit knowledge spreads through demonstration.

sharp_disagreements.title: Your Strength as a Rationalist
sharp_disagreements.quote: Anyone reporting sudden chest pains should have been hauled off by an ambulance instantly.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: EMS non-transport of chest-pain patients is common; the narrator's ambulance model was simply wrong.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay says model or story is wrong; confusion flagged both errors, so Fable strengthens the lesson.

sharp_disagreements.title: Your Strength as a Rationalist
sharp_disagreements.quote: And the Medical Establishment was always right. Every single time.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Diagnostic errors and missed MIs are common; "always right" generalizes from a tiny personal sample.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Line is the narrator confessing his mistaken induction; Fable restates the essay's own point.

sharp_disagreements.title: Your Strength as a Rationalist
sharp_disagreements.quote: Alas, belief is easier than disbelief
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Spinozan default appears only without background knowledge; anecdote shows motivated reasoning instead.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Richter's own condition (no relevant knowledge) fits the IRC story; both mechanisms named by essay.

sharp_disagreements.title: Explain/Worship/Ignore?
sharp_disagreements.quote: There—I just hit Worship.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Agrippa's trilemma: every explanatory chain ends somewhere; taxonomy brands all coherent stopping points as bad.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Explain button means keep asking; Worship is sacralizing the endpoint, not accepting brute facts.

sharp_disagreements.title: Explain/Worship/Ignore?
sharp_disagreements.quote: this question having never occurred to him before
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: No ethnography supports the incurious wise man; CSR says supernatural beliefs are not explanatory answers.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Boyer's account fits the parable; supernatural answers stopping at the next question is the essay's verdict.

sharp_disagreements.title: Failing to Learn from History
sharp_disagreements.quote: My younger self did not realize that solving a mystery should make it feel less confusing.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Quantum mechanics solved mysteries yet stayed confusing; felt mundanity is a poor criterion of explanation.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Criterion concerns predictive confusion, not strangeness; residual confusion in QM marks the unsolved part.

sharp_disagreements.title: Failing to Learn from History
sharp_disagreements.quote: Only then did I realize how reasonable vitalism had seemed at the time
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Contradicts earlier essay calling vitalists proud of ignorance; this essay quietly retracts it.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Same error seen outside and inside; essay explicitly withdraws only the character-flaw lesson.

sharp_disagreements.title: Failing to Learn from History
sharp_disagreements.quote: right up until science finally solved them
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Origin of life and other old mysteries unsolved; induction from solved mysteries is survivorship.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Vitalism's question was answered; origin of life is different; no mysterious answer ever paid rent.

sharp_disagreements.title: Fake Causality
sharp_disagreements.quote: You couldn’t even use phlogiston theory to say what you ought not to see; it could explain everything.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Phlogiston prohibited outcomes and made advance predictions; one prohibited result (weight gain) killed it.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Phlogiston survived the weight anomaly via ad hoc fixes, exactly the essay's complaint (Lavoisier).

sharp_disagreements.title: Fake Causality
sharp_disagreements.quote: if we already know that the sidewalk is wet, learning that the sidewalk is slippery tells us nothing more about whether it rained
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: People systematically violate the causal Markov condition (Rehder & Burnett; Rottman & Hastie).
sharp_disagreements.gist: Markov violations support "used badly" and imply richer graphs, per Rehder & Burnett's own explanation.

sharp_disagreements.title: Fake Causality
sharp_disagreements.quote: A properly designed AI would notice the problem instantly.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Exact Bayes-net inference is NP-hard; loopy networks double-count; "instantly" is textbook polytree thinking.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Blocking evidence reuse needs only provenance tracking; junction tree never double-counts; held-out sets do this.

sharp_disagreements.title: Fake Explanations
sharp_disagreements.quote: Taken from Joachim Verhagen
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Founding anecdote comes from a science jokes file; generalizing from it is fictional evidence.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Anecdote is openly a joke; the claim rests on Force Concept Inventory evidence of verbal-only learning.

sharp_disagreements.title: Fake Explanations
sharp_disagreements.quote: It is anticipation-isomorphic to saying “magic.”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Heat conduction is false, not empty; essay conflates falsified hypotheses with maximum-entropy ones.
sharp_disagreements.gist: "Used in such fashion": essay says conduction is false as prediction, empty as used to explain the opposite.

sharp_disagreements.title: Fake Explanations
sharp_disagreements.quote: Some students guessed convection of air currents, and others guessed strange metals in the plate.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Rapid hypothesis generation is the signature of expert reasoning; "I don't know" generates no test.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay prescribes hypothesis generation; faults students for failing to notice the anomaly.

sharp_disagreements.title: Guessing the Teacher’s Password
sharp_disagreements.quote: until I saw that it was embarrassingly obvious
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Essay's criterion for understanding is a feeling of obviousness, which the sequence elsewhere distrusts.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Criterion is three days of derivation, the very production test Rozenblit & Keil use.

sharp_disagreements.title: Guessing the Teacher’s Password
sharp_disagreements.quote: putting in numbers and getting out results that control your anticipation of particular experiences
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Physics-education research: plugging numbers in coexists with conceptual misunderstanding; wrong criterion.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay counts qualitative anticipation (flowing match) as understanding; FCI measures exactly that.

sharp_disagreements.title: Guessing the Teacher’s Password
sharp_disagreements.quote: which must be the correct answer because the teacher heard a physicist emit the same sound-vibrations
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Mocking belief via physicist testimony contradicts What Is Evidence?; testimony is rational justification.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Child had no belief to receive; Hardwig's trust requires understanding the proposition.

sharp_disagreements.title: Lawful Uncertainty
sharp_disagreements.quote: Despite feedback through a thousand trials, subjects cannot bring themselves to believe that the situation is one in which they cannot predict.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: With incentives most subjects converge to maximizing; matching is a defensible pattern-detection strategy.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Shanks shows matching is correctable error; essay endorses pattern search while betting blue.

sharp_disagreements.title: Lawful Uncertainty
sharp_disagreements.quote: Decision theory does not burst into flames and die when faced with an opponent who disobeys decision theory.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Against an opponent decision theory often prescribes randomizing; slogan reverses in adversarial games.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Mixed strategies are lawfully computed best responses; essay's slogan targets randomness replacing calculation.

sharp_disagreements.title: Lawful Uncertainty
sharp_disagreements.quote: How many theories of AI?
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: SGD, dropout, temperature sampling and randomized exploration succeeded; never-randomize is false for AI.
sharp_disagreements.gist: AI randomness buys information, saves compute or patches models; none applies to the card task.

sharp_disagreements.title: Making History Available
sharp_disagreements.quote: In our ancestral environment, there were no movies; what you saw with your own eyes was true.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Eyewitness perception is unreliable and ancestral environments were narrative-saturated; just-so story.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Eyewitness errors concern memory for faces, not seeing nonevents; essay deliberately dissolves the distinction.

sharp_disagreements.title: Making History Available
sharp_disagreements.quote: I should try to think as if everything I read about in history books had actually happened to me.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Imagining events creates false memories; vivid historical analogies are a documented source of policy error.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay's "I wasn't there" and thousand-peasants reweighting; Neustadt & May prescribe broad history too.

sharp_disagreements.title: Making History Available
sharp_disagreements.quote: So many mistakes, made over and over and over again, because I did not remember making them, in every era I never lived
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Mistakes recur because historical lessons are ambiguous, not forgotten; intensity cannot resolve interpretation.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay's lessons are base rates, e.g. the world changing unpredictably, not ambiguous causal lessons.

sharp_disagreements.title: My Wild and Reckless Youth
sharp_disagreements.quote: This required neurons to maintain a certain degree of quantum coherence, which was something you could look for, and find or not find.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Orch-OR was tested and failed by Traditional means (Tegmark 2000); Bayes contributed nothing.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Complaint is about thirty years of leniency; Orch-OR survived Tegmark; Bayes would discount it earlier.

sharp_disagreements.title: My Wild and Reckless Youth
sharp_disagreements.quote: Do not attempt long chains of reasoning or complicated plans.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Advice against long chains contradicts the intelligence-explosion argument the book builds on.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Advice qualified by "pinned down overwhelmingly"; short AI-risk argument needs no long chain.

sharp_disagreements.title: My Wild and Reckless Youth
sharp_disagreements.quote: if a hypothesis does not today have a favorable likelihood ratio over “I don’t know,”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: "I don't know" has no well-defined likelihood; catch-all problem makes the test unrunnable.
sharp_disagreements.gist: "I don't know" is a broad predictive distribution; merely permissive hypotheses get likelihood ratio one.

sharp_disagreements.title: Mysterious Answers to Mysterious Questions
sharp_disagreements.quote: Lord Kelvin sure did get a tremendous emotional kick out of not knowing something.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Kelvin's vitalism was a testable thermodynamic claim refuted by calorimetry, not cherished ignorance.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Kelvin's vital principle directed motion, invisible to energy audits; calorimetry left it untouched.

sharp_disagreements.title: Mysterious Answers to Mysterious Questions
sharp_disagreements.quote: Second, the hypothesis has no moving parts
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: "No moving parts" condemns the gene, caloric, ether and neutrino, the standard successful move of science.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Signs are conjunctive; gene, neutrino and caloric predicted, were searched for, and fail the other signs.

sharp_disagreements.title: Positive Bias: Look into the Dark
sharp_disagreements.quote: For by instinct, we human beings only live in half the world.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Positive testing is near-optimal in natural environments (Klayman & Ha); DAX/MED framing triples success.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Klayman & Ha mark where positive testing fails, fake explanations included; DAX/MED shows the prescription working.

sharp_disagreements.title: Positive Bias: Look into the Dark
sharp_disagreements.quote: but phlogiston theory could just as well have explained the flame not going out
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Phlogiston's finite-capacity air predicted flames go out in sealed vessels; it prohibited the other outcome.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Air capacity was a parameter fitted after the fact to explain either outcome, per Fable's own Priestley.

sharp_disagreements.title: Positive Bias: Look into the Dark
sharp_disagreements.quote: I replied that non-superconductivity and non-ferromagnetism were also examples of emergence, which was the problem.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Essay misreads emergence claim; both phases are emergent and the theory predicts which obtains.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Predictions come from BCS and order-parameter models; the label "emergent" discriminates nothing.

sharp_disagreements.title: Say Not “Complexity”
sharp_disagreements.quote: advocating that the Internet would “wake up” and become an AI when it became “sufficiently complex.”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Scaling generic architectures on Internet text produced intelligence-like behavior without a worked-out mechanism.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Scaling laws are quantitative predictions from a specific mechanism; the Internet did not wake up.

sharp_disagreements.title: Say Not “Complexity”
sharp_disagreements.quote: That was when I thought to myself, “Maybe this one is teachable.”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Student repeating "emergence" is guessing the teacher's password, the test the sequence condemns.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Marcello applied the principle to a new word and changed his next step: understanding, not a password.

sharp_disagreements.title: Science as Attire
sharp_disagreements.quote: It would be worse than finding rabbit fossils in the pre-Cambrian.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Horizontal gene transfer and endosymbiosis were absorbed, not falsifying; theories accommodate anomalies.
sharp_disagreements.gist: HGT and endosymbiosis import gradually evolved machinery; the ban is on complexity from nowhere.

sharp_disagreements.title: Science as Attire
sharp_disagreements.quote: Their devastating critiques consist purely of comparisons to apocalyptic literature, rather than, say, known laws which prohibit such an outcome.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Asymmetric burden: proponents had no model of intelligence either; "no law forbids it" was rejected for Storm.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Impossibility claims need a bound; nobody has one, and AI systems now beat humans in many domains.

sharp_disagreements.title: Semantic Stopsigns
sharp_disagreements.quote: How well have liberal democracies performed, historically, on problems this tricky?
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Liberal democracies have a strong record (Sen, Acemoglu); diagnostic can't tell compression from stopped thinking.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Objection is to treating the question as illegitimate; Sen and Acemoglu are answers to the next question.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Futility of Emergence
sharp_disagreements.quote: Taken literally, that description fits every phenomenon in our universe above the level of individual quarks
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Essay attacks a Wikipedia sentence, ignoring technical emergence in physics and philosophy, which has predictive content.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay explicitly permits 'emerges from' a specific model; the physics literature is that permitted usage.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Futility of Emergence
sharp_disagreements.quote: Human intelligence is a magical product of neurons firing.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Emergent and magical license different inferences; substitution test uses sentences chosen to be empty.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Fable had to supply the content itself; the deletion test forces exactly that, so it worked.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Futility of Emergence
sharp_disagreements.quote: I have lost track of how many times I have heard people say, “Intelligence is an emergent phenomenon!”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: LLM 'emergent abilities' became a falsifiable technical claim, contradicting the prediction that emergence is only a curiosity-stopper.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Schaeffer et al. dissolved LLM emergent abilities as metric artefacts, vindicating the essay.

sharp_disagreements.title: Truly Part of You
sharp_disagreements.quote: Could I regenerate this knowledge if it were somehow deleted from my mind?
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Regeneration test would exclude nearly all testimonial knowledge; social epistemology treats testimony as normal.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Test targets understanding not origin; generation effect and self-explanation research support it.

sharp_disagreements.title: Truly Part of You
sharp_disagreements.quote: If all proofs of the Pythagorean Theorem were deleted from my mind, could I re-prove it? I think so.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Regeneration test is untested self-report, vulnerable to the illusion of explanatory depth.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay says to put it to the test; retrieval practice supports regeneration as remedy for explanatory-depth illusion.

sharp_disagreements.title: “Science” as Curiosity-Stopper
sharp_disagreements.quote: But because someone else knows, it devalues the knowledge in your eyes.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Curiosity literature says known, reachable answers raise curiosity; the essay's psychology is reversed.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Sloman & Rabb 2016: being told scientists understand closes the felt gap without the answer.

sharp_disagreements.title: “Science” as Curiosity-Stopper
sharp_disagreements.quote: Is this not spite?
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Walking past known answers is prioritization, which the essay concedes; curiosity tracks expected value.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay separates instrumental goods (division of labor) from the raw emotion; prioritization already granted.

sharp_disagreements.title: 0 And 1 Are Not Probabilities
sharp_disagreements.quote: So I propose that it makes sense to say that 1 and 0 are not in the probabilities
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Proposal is the 1950s norm of regularity, impossible in infinite spaces; die example conflates model tautology with claim.
sharp_disagreements.gist: The norm is Lindley's Cromwell's rule; measure-zero points aren't held propositions; model uncertainty is the point.

sharp_disagreements.title: 0 And 1 Are Not Probabilities
sharp_disagreements.quote: The main reason this would upset probability theorists is that we would need to rederive theorems previously obtained by assuming that we can marginalize over a joint probability by adding up all the pieces and having them sum to 1.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Dropping normalization removes Bayes' theorem itself; Popper functions already handle probability-zero conditioning.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Normalization stays within models; Shimony's tempered personalism endorses the catch-all hypothesis.

sharp_disagreements.title: 0 And 1 Are Not Probabilities
sharp_disagreements.quote: Just as there are mathematicians who refuse to believe in the law of the excluded middle or infinite sets, I would like to be a probability theorist who doesn’t believe in absolute certainty.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: No system offered; the defensible core is regularity for contingent propositions, not reform of the number line.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Fable grants the substantive regularity claim; logical induction later supplied the missing system.

sharp_disagreements.title: Absolute Authority
sharp_disagreements.quote: In the world of the unenlightened ones, there is authority and un-authority.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Developmental research shows 'science is probabilistic' pushes absolutists into multiplist relativism, not evaluativism.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay warns against the multiplist slide and prescribes the evaluativist position Kuhn et al. describe.

sharp_disagreements.title: Absolute Authority
sharp_disagreements.quote: They will accept the first half of the statement as a confession of guilt; and dismiss the second half as a flailing attempt to accuse everyone else to avoid judgment.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Communicating uncertainty barely costs trust (van der Bles 2020); only expert disagreement does.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Van der Bles found verbal uncertainty hurts trust while numeric doesn't, matching the essay's distinction.

sharp_disagreements.title: Absolute Authority
sharp_disagreements.quote: If you take one hundred people and ask them each to make a statement of which they are “absolutely certain,” how many of these statements will be correct? Not one hundred.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Overconfidence came from hard experimenter-chosen items; self-chosen certainties would score near one hundred.
sharp_disagreements.gist: 'Not one hundred' needs one error; Fable's 'near one hundred' concedes it; misconceptions supply errors.

sharp_disagreements.title: Absolute Authority
sharp_disagreements.quote: If anything, the statements that people are really fanatic about are far less likely to be correct than statements like “the Sun is larger than the Moon” that seem too obvious to get excited about.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Untested claim that fanatic beliefs are far less likely correct; argument only shows they're contested.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Fanatic certainties come paired with opposites, so at most half are right; follows arithmetically.

sharp_disagreements.title: Absolute Authority
sharp_disagreements.quote: it means you think you could make one million equally strong independent statements, one after the other, over the course of a solid year or so, and be wrong, on average, around once
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Million-statements gloss is frequentist, contradicting the sequence's Bayesianism, and is impossible to satisfy.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Dawid's theorem makes calibration a Bayesian property; the million-statements gloss illustrates it.

sharp_disagreements.title: But There’s Still a Chance, Right?
sharp_disagreements.quote: they have undoubtedly been wrong more often than once in
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Model-uncertainty sentence undercuts the essay: the interlocutor's 'still a chance' was right.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Model uncertainty releases mass to other errors, not to coincidence; still a chance to ignore.

sharp_disagreements.title: But There’s Still a Chance, Right?
sharp_disagreements.quote: if you can’t ignore a likelihood of one over googol because you want to, you can’t ignore a likelihood of 0.9 because you want to
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Essay uses 'likelihood' loosely as posterior; a likelihood alone is meaningless without the alternative.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Rewritten with likelihood ratios the argument survives; 'because you want to' is operative.

sharp_disagreements.title: How to Convince Me That 2 + 2 = 3
sharp_disagreements.quote: In the second case, I would think it more likely that they had messed with my arithmetic recall than that 2 + 2 actually equalled 4.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: The essay's own sentence shows arithmetic is the last belief to go; Quine and Frege already answer it.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Fable misreads the sentence: the author would conclude 2+2=3 and the memory of 4 was implanted.

sharp_disagreements.title: How to Convince Me That 2 + 2 = 3
sharp_disagreements.quote: Presumably it would be the same sort of situation causally responsible for producing your current belief in Christianity: We would push you screaming out of the uterus of a Muslim woman
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Upbringing challenge is a symmetric genetic fallacy; religiousness partly heritable and conversion common.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Question is counterfactual sensitivity, not genetic; Lofland & Stark show conversion runs through social bonds.

sharp_disagreements.title: How to Convince Me That 2 + 2 = 3
sharp_disagreements.quote: The evidential crossfire of physical observation, mental visualization, and social agreement.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Visualization and social agreement aren't independent witnesses; essay's arithmetic belief is as unconditional as anyone's.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay distinguishes unconditional facts from unconditional beliefs; its witnesses are entangled, the congregation's aren't.

sharp_disagreements.title: Infinite Certainty
sharp_disagreements.quote: I am not going to discuss the actual experiments that have been done on calibration
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Calibration literature shows a hard-easy effect; applied to 2+2=4 it predicts underconfidence.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay concedes 99.99% for 2+2=4; Erev et al. show overconfidence at the top of the scale.

sharp_disagreements.title: Infinite Certainty
sharp_disagreements.quote: I don’t think you could get up to 99.99% confidence for assertions like “53 is a prime number.”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Credence below 1 in a theorem violates the probability axioms the essay invokes; needs logical induction.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Logical induction formalizes the essay's position; Hacking 1967 named the bounded-reasoner problem.

sharp_disagreements.title: Infinite Certainty
sharp_disagreements.quote: Assert a confidence of (1 − 1⁄googolplex) and your ego far exceeds that of mental patients who think they’re God.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: A credence is not an ego claim; frequency verification isn't what subjectivist credence means.
sharp_disagreements.gist: By Dawid's theorem an extreme credence commits you to expecting hardware reliability no brain has.

sharp_disagreements.title: Lotteries: A Waste of Hope
sharp_disagreements.quote: If not for the lottery, maybe they would fantasize about going to technical school, or opening their own business, or getting a promotion at work
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Oettingen finds positive fantasies about achievable goals also reduce effort; proposed harm mechanism unsupported.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Oettingen's mental contrasting completes the essay: achievable fantasies can become plans, lottery ones cannot.

sharp_disagreements.title: Lotteries: A Waste of Hope
sharp_disagreements.quote: This seems sufficient to explain the popularity of lotteries.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Relative-poverty and fairness manipulations change lottery buying; innumeracy is not sufficient explanation.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Haisley et al.'s bundling study shows presentation of arithmetic changes demand; status amplifies the error.

sharp_disagreements.title: New Improved Lottery
sharp_disagreements.quote: between zero chance of becoming wealthy, and epsilon chance, there is an order-of-epsilon difference. If you doubt this, let epsilon equal one over googolplex.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Googolplex substitution changes the subject; commenter meant decision weights, where the possibility effect applies.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Commenter spoke of chances; the possibility effect is the bias diagnosed, and googolplex is a diagnostic.

sharp_disagreements.title: New Improved Lottery
sharp_disagreements.quote: You buy in once, for a single dollar, and get not just a few days of epsilon chance of becoming rich, but a few years of epsilon.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: The satirized product exists as Premium Bonds and prize-linked savings, and it benefits savers.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Premium Bonds and prize-linked savings prove lotteries are overpriced and reduce lottery spending.

sharp_disagreements.title: New Improved Lottery
sharp_disagreements.quote: Yep, offering people tempting daydreams that will not actually happen sure is a valuable service, all right.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Anticipation needs scheduled resolution (Loewenstein 1987); weekly draw is what the savoring model predicts.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Premium Bonds keep scheduled draws yet return stake; savoring doesn't justify the state's take.

sharp_disagreements.title: New Improved Lottery
sharp_disagreements.quote: The alternative is that consumers are making mistakes, and we all know that can’t happen.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Sarcasm targets a position no economist held; essay assumes rather than argues paternalism.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Sarcasm answers a revealed-preference argument actually made; Fable grants the overcharge.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Fallacy of Gray
sharp_disagreements.quote: many bloggers have said of Overcoming Bias: “It is impossible, no one can completely eliminate bias.”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Critics' real objection is that debiasing can't be self-measured given the bias blind spot; essay dodges it.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Bias reduction is measurable via scoring and forecasting tournaments (Mellers 2014); Morewedge reduced blind spot.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Fallacy of Gray
sharp_disagreements.quote: then in many cases I don’t think it’s unreasonable to call the output “straightforward”—even in economics
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Economists' policy positions track values, not parameter estimates; evidence favors Cowen over Hanson.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Gordon & Dahl's consensus supports 'in many cases'; values drive disagreement only where parameters are uncertain.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Fallacy of Gray
sharp_disagreements.quote: It’s a most peculiar psychology—this business of “Science is based on faith too, so there!”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Lay trust in science resembles faith; predictive success faces the pessimistic meta-induction; 'devil's bargain' is mind-reading.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Epistemic status of science differs from how laypeople hold it; Worrall's structural realism answers meta-induction.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Fallacy of Gray
sharp_disagreements.quote: Or even if not, we can still compare shades, and say “it is darker” or “it is lighter.”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Comparing shades assumes one dimension; multiple biases and moral incommensurability defeat 'darker or lighter'.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Probability is scalar; Pareto dominance suffices to refute universal levelling even with incommensurable cases.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Proper Use of Humility
sharp_disagreements.quote: Does acting this way make you stronger, or weaker?
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: 'Stronger or weaker' is undefined and reproduces the author's verdicts; it is just an expected-value calculation.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Test is defined by specific actions; replacing virtue with a decision rule is the point and excludes empty modesty.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Proper Use of Humility
sharp_disagreements.quote: Scientific humility is something you would practice even if you were alone in a spacesuit, light years from Earth with no one watching
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Solitary self-correction is where the bias blind spot is worst; science's self-correction is social.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Spacesuit contrasts motives; procedures work alone; Trouche et al. show solitary self-evaluation catches invalid arguments.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Proper Use of Humility
sharp_disagreements.quote: because physicists have this arrogant idea that their models should work all the time, not just most of the time, they follow up on small flaws
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Mercury's perihelion and the solar neutrino deficit were tolerated for decades, not promptly followed up.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Vulcan hunts, Newcomb's remeasurement and decades of neutrino experiments are the follow-up the essay describes.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Proper Use of Humility
sharp_disagreements.quote: And the greater the inconvenience of changing one’s mind, the more effort people will expend on the proof.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Wood & Porter: corrections generally accepted, backfire not reproduced; Galbraith's aphorism overstated.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Swire and Nyhan: voters accept corrections but keep supporting the candidate, Galbraith as a finding.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Third Alternative
sharp_disagreements.quote: If Santa-belief is destroyed by truth, the children will lose their sense of wonder and stop behaving nicely.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Children discovering Santa's truth react neutrally or positively; the feared harm was looked for and absent.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay's method defeats Noble-Lie arguments even where premises hold; Fable's fix works in one case only.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Third Alternative
sharp_disagreements.quote: It’s amazing how many Noble Liars and their ilk are eager to embrace ethical violations
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Prosocial lies are judged moral and increase trust (Levine & Schweitzer); motive attribution is untested.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Noble Lies are paternalistic lies, judged unethical (Lupoli et al. 2018), unlike white lies.

sharp_disagreements.title: Your Rationality Is My Business
sharp_disagreements.quote: It is somewhat inconsistent for your utility function to contain a negative term for anyone else’s utility function having a term for someone else’s utility function.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Preferences over others' preferences are consistent meta-preferences (Sen 1977); 'inconsistent' is wrong.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Inconsistency is performative, marked 'somewhat', and the essay itself calls it only a snappy comeback.

sharp_disagreements.title: Your Rationality Is My Business
sharp_disagreements.quote: If there are any true Relativists or Selfishes, we do not hear them—they remain silent, non-players.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: No-true-Scotsman against relativists; framework relativists can argue; motive read off behavior.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Relativists arguing across frameworks claim non-relative authority; the Theaetetus argument stands.

sharp_disagreements.title: Your Rationality Is My Business
sharp_disagreements.quote: Let’s argue against bad ideas but not set their bearers on fire.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Essay gives a mission statement instead of Clifford's stronger ethics-of-belief argument.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay shares Clifford's argument in milder form, claiming only standing to argue and conceding gradation.

sharp_disagreements.title: Argument Screens Off Authority
sharp_disagreements.quote: P(truth|argument, expert) = P(truth|argument).
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Screening off holds only for complete arguments; experts' unseen evidence keeps authority informative, as essay concedes.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay stipulates complete arguments and treats unseen evidence as partial screening; checked proofs screen off authors.

sharp_disagreements.title: Argument Screens Off Authority
sharp_disagreements.quote: Assuming that Arthur is knowledgeable enough to understand all the technical arguments—otherwise they’re just impressive noises
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Laypeople usually can't evaluate technical arguments, so the assumption rarely holds and credentials matter.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay itself says unevaluated arguments are mystical syllables resting on authority; Dunning-Kruger shaky.

sharp_disagreements.title: Argument Screens Off Authority
sharp_disagreements.quote: But this slight strength of authority is only ceteris paribus, and can easily be overwhelmed by stronger arguments.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: 'Slight' authority is asserted not derived; expert likelihood ratios can be large.
sharp_disagreements.gist: After hearing the argument the residual likelihood ratio approaches one; 'slight' follows from the theorem.

sharp_disagreements.title: Hug the Query
sharp_disagreements.quote: he probably doesn’t have any apart from his own incredulity
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Kelvin 'impossible' quote is apocryphal; the Wrights were systematic experimenters, not lucky amateurs.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay paraphrases the attitude; Fable's documented 1896 letter and wind tunnel confirm the essay's contrast.

sharp_disagreements.title: Hug the Query
sharp_disagreements.quote: If you actually watch the plane fly, the calculations themselves become moot for many purposes, and Kelvin’s authority not even worth considering.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Few watched the Wrights fly before 1908; for most people the choice remained between authorities.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay concedes you can't always check; Le Mans 1908 shows one observation ended years of dispute.

sharp_disagreements.title: Hug the Query
sharp_disagreements.quote: It’s a theorem of these causal graphs that you can never get more information from distant nodes, than from strictly closer nodes that screen off the distant ones.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Data-processing inequality applies to screening-off nodes, not 'closer' ones; distance has no epistemic meaning.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Sentence explicitly restricts to screening-off nodes; Fable substitutes a different query for the Wright example.

sharp_disagreements.title: Human Evil and Muddled Thinking
sharp_disagreements.quote: Orwell knew that muddled language is muddled thinking
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Muddled-language-is-muddled-thinking is strong Whorf, rejected; language effects small and domain-specific.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Claim is euphemism muting revulsion, not strong Whorf; Bandura's dehumanizing-label studies measure it.

sharp_disagreements.title: Human Evil and Muddled Thinking
sharp_disagreements.quote: Except for a few natural catastrophes, every great woe has been driven by a stupidity.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Largest mortality events (plagues, Columbian epidemics) weren't driven by stupidity; claim unfalsifiable otherwise.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Natural catastrophes are few by count and had human amplifiers; the war metaphor targets our own errors.

sharp_disagreements.title: Policy Debates Should Not Appear One-Sided
sharp_disagreements.quote: But, as a matter of simple fact, she’s still going to die.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Policy consequence treated as one-sided fact; the mother of five is an identifiable-victim device.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Existence of a victim differs from net effect; the vivid victim was a deliberate test of readers' reflex.

sharp_disagreements.title: Policy Debates Should Not Appear One-Sided
sharp_disagreements.quote: Can you imagine a politician saying that? Neither can I.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Regulators routinely trade lives for benefits using value of statistical life; not unspeakable.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay anticipates journal-article VSL analyses; its point is what politicians can't say aloud, as Fable confirms.

sharp_disagreements.title: Politics is the Mind-Killer
sharp_disagreements.quote: The evolutionary reasons for this are so obvious as to be worth belaboring: In the ancestral environment, politics was a matter of life and death.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Evolutionary story is untested just-so; identity-protective cognition is an ignored present-tense alternative.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Identity cognition is proximate, coalitional adaptation ultimate; Mercier & Sperber and Kurzban et al. support it.

sharp_disagreements.title: Politics is the Mind-Killer
sharp_disagreements.quote: People who would be level-headed about evenhandedly weighing all sides of an issue in their professional life as scientists, can suddenly turn into slogan-chanting zombies
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Deliberation experiments show political opinion change is common; essay generalizes from online comment sections.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Deliberative polls remove partisan cues; Cohen 2003 shows party labels override policy content.

sharp_disagreements.title: Politics is the Mind-Killer
sharp_disagreements.quote: it’s a terrible domain in which to learn rationality, or discuss rationality, unless all the discussants are already rational
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Far-transfer pessimism means avoiding political examples avoids practice where reasoning fails.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Learning under low identity threat then transferring is supported by self-affirmation research and Morewedge.

sharp_disagreements.title: Rationality and the English Language
sharp_disagreements.quote: Passive voice removes the actor, leaving only the acted-upon.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Pullum shows the passive is often clearer; concealment lives in nouns, not the passive.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay's examples are agentless passives and it names nominalization; Doyen shows the hidden agent mattered.

sharp_disagreements.title: Rationality and the English Language
sharp_disagreements.quote: Meaning does not excuse impact!
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: 'Meaning does not excuse impact' licenses the affect heuristic, with no criterion for vivid truth vs manipulation.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Rule addresses writers' responsibility; awareness resists transportation; concreteness matching events is the criterion.

sharp_disagreements.title: Rationality and the English Language
sharp_disagreements.quote: Orwell was the outraged opponent of totalitarianism and the muddy thinking in which evil cloaks itself—which is how Orwell’s writings on language ended up as classic rationalist documents
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Orwell's linguistics is Whorfian and fared badly; Klemperer saw through Nazi euphemisms.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Klemperer's LTI documents Nazi words infecting opponents' thinking, supporting Orwell's habit-based claim.

sharp_disagreements.title: Reversed Stupidity Is Not Intelligence
sharp_disagreements.quote: If you want to argue against transhumanism or the intelligence explosion, you have to directly challenge the arguments of Nick Bostrom or Eliezer Yudkowsky post-2003.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Strongest-advocate rule applied self-servingly; weak-man literature warns of disowning members' actual claims.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Bostrom named first; post-2003 excludes abandoned positions; rule targets ideas, movements judged elsewhere.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Scales of Justice, the Notebook of Rationality
sharp_disagreements.quote: If Justitia must consider any more complex issue, she should relinquish her scales or relinquish her sword.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Expected utility aggregates considerations to one number; scales are needed for complex choices and misdescribe binary jury decisions.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Expected utility is not a two-pan scale; facts-first then aggregation is the essay's own argument.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Scales of Justice, the Notebook of Rationality
sharp_disagreements.quote: At the end of the debate, the speaker who has scored more points is, obviously, the winner; so everything that speaker says must be true, and everything the loser says must be wrong.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Scorekeeping audience is an invented caricature; debate research shows small, reinforcing effects instead.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Next paragraph's Finucane study supplies evidence; Fable's reinforcing-debate effects show the combat model working.

sharp_disagreements.title: A Rational Argument
sharp_disagreements.quote: It is no longer possible for the voters to condition on the facts alone; they must condition on the additional fact of their presentation, and infer the existence of hidden evidence.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Milgrom unraveling: skeptical voters infer omissions, so selective disclosure isn't deception; essay's standard is stricter than needed.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Milgrom proves the essay's own inference; Jin, Luca & Martin show real receivers are insufficiently skeptical.

sharp_disagreements.title: A Rational Argument
sharp_disagreements.quote: Whatever actually decides your bottom line, is the only thing you can honestly write on the lines above.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Nisbett & Wilson: people cannot access what decided their bottom line, so the honesty standard is unmeetable.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Written checklist routes around introspection; Dawes's improper linear models show printed rules cause conclusions.

sharp_disagreements.title: Avoiding Your Belief’s Real Weak Points
sharp_disagreements.quote: You don’t even ask whether the incident reflects poorly on God, so there’s no need to quickly blurt out “The ways of God are mysterious!”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: The rabbis did ask: Megillah 10b rebukes angels singing at Egyptians' drowning; wine drops embody the objection.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay credits rabbis' sympathy but says they stop short of 'This is not right'; Megillah 10b fits exactly.

sharp_disagreements.title: Avoiding Your Belief’s Real Weak Points
sharp_disagreements.quote: Punch yourself in the solar plexus. Stick a knife in your heart, and wiggle to widen the hole.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Only structured consider-the-opposite works; dwelling on painful material resembles rumination, not a method.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay includes a structured consider-the-opposite step; experiential avoidance predicts worse outcomes, exposure works.

sharp_disagreements.title: Dark Side Epistemology
sharp_disagreements.quote: “Everyone has a right to their own opinion.” When you think about it, where was that proverb generated? Is it something that someone would say in the course of protecting a truth, or in the course of protecting from the truth?
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Proverb descends from liberal toleration (Locke, Mill); essay commits the genetic fallacy it forbids.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Question concerns use of proverb to end arguments; Mill himself required opinions to stay exposed to argument.

sharp_disagreements.title: Dark Side Epistemology
sharp_disagreements.quote: A single Lie That Must Be Protected can block someone’s progress into advanced rationality.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Religiosity-IQ correlation only about -0.2 and compartmentalization is normal; metastasizing-lie mechanism unmeasured.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Pennycook et al. 2020: belief that beliefs should follow evidence predicts lower religious belief beyond ability.

sharp_disagreements.title: Dark Side Epistemology
sharp_disagreements.quote: Or you could just lie about evolutionary theory, which is the path taken by most creationists.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Most creationists are sincere; childhood teleology is default, so the lie-propagation mechanism doesn't fit.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay covers self-deception; Pandas drafts and Kitzmiller perjury document the original lies.

sharp_disagreements.title: Entangled Truths, Contagious Lies
sharp_disagreements.quote: But the Great Web is very commonly underestimated.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Diary studies show everyday lies rarely detected; entanglement risk is overstated except where institutions look.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Liars can't know detection; Park et al. show lies found via third-party evidence; genetic genealogy expands the web.

sharp_disagreements.title: Entangled Truths, Contagious Lies
sharp_disagreements.quote: A student of evolutionary biology can see the design signature of natural selection on every wolf that chases a rabbit; and every rabbit that runs away; and every bee that stings instead of broadcasting a polite warning—but the deceptions of creationists sound plausible to them, I’m sure.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Creationism is the cognitive default (Evans 2001), not deception; no first lie for contagion to spread from.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Sentence names deceivers and the deceived; Discovery Institute Wedge document shows the deliberate strategy.

sharp_disagreements.title: Fake Justification
sharp_disagreements.quote: It’s improbable that you used mistaken reasoning, yet made no mistakes.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Heuristics routinely reach correct answers (take-the-best); the dice analogy conflates criterion choice with process reliability.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay targets unrelated processes; take-the-best tracks criterion, and dice sentence exempts correlated processes.

sharp_disagreements.title: Fake Justification
sharp_disagreements.quote: The standard atheist reply is given by Sam Harris: “You and I both know that it would take us five minutes to produce a book that offers a more coherent and compassionate morality than the Bible does.”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Harris's reply answers a claim believers didn't make; reverence is a communal commitment, not literary judgment.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay reports the ethical-advice claim; Fable's social-commitment reading is the essay's fake-justification thesis.

sharp_disagreements.title: Is That Your True Rejection?
sharp_disagreements.quote: then I suspect that the point at which the average person will actually start to grant credence overriding their initial impression, purely because of academic credentials, is somewhere around the Nobel Laureate level
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Source-credibility research shows credentials persuade at far lower levels than Nobel laureate.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Hovland & Weiss sleeper effect erodes credential advantage; Kahan et al. 2011 show credentials ignored against priors.

sharp_disagreements.title: Is That Your True Rejection?
sharp_disagreements.quote: But did the same people who said, “Come back when you have a PhD,” actually change their minds at all about molecular nanotechnology? Not so far as I ever heard.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Critics raised technical objections (Smalley, NRC 2006); recoding them as pretexts makes the framework unfalsifiable.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Smalley attacked a design Drexler didn't propose; NRC found feasibility unsettled; essay's list includes the other side knowing more.

sharp_disagreements.title: Is That Your True Rejection?
sharp_disagreements.quote: It has similarly been a general rule with the Machine Intelligence Research Institute that, whatever it is we’re supposed to do to be more credible, when we actually do it, nothing much changes.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: No credibility measure; demands met with substitutes (OpenCog affiliation), so critics' continued doubt is reasonable.
sharp_disagreements.gist: OpenCog was the institute's own effort; minds changed only when AI capabilities arrived (2023 CAIS statement).

sharp_disagreements.title: Knowing About Biases Can Hurt People
sharp_disagreements.quote: one of the primary ways that people with high mental agility end up stupid, in Stanovich’s “dysrationalia” sense of stupidity
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Stanovich found ability reduces most biases; only myside bias is independent; dysrationalia doesn't mean agility causes stupidity.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Stanovich & West 2008 found between-subject biases independent of ability; dysrationalia usage matches Stanovich's.

sharp_disagreements.title: Knowing About Biases Can Hurt People
sharp_disagreements.quote: Whether I do it on paper, or in speech, I now try to never mention calibration and overconfidence unless I have first talked about disconfirmation bias, motivated skepticism, sophisticated arguers, and dysrationalia in the mentally agile.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Lecture-ordering prescription untested; forewarning about biases has the weakest debiasing record.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay's approach is self-directed training, not bare forewarning; Morewedge et al. 2015 show such training persists.

sharp_disagreements.title: One Argument Against An Army
sharp_disagreements.quote: Again, these three arguments outweigh the first (by three arguments against one argument), so you keep your belief that Sylvania is responsible.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Example counts arguments; likelihood ratios multiply, Sylvanian signs are correlated, and mechanism objection attacks the prior.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Tallying is the mocked Freedonian's voice; essay prescribes integrating evidence via likelihood ratios.

sharp_disagreements.title: One Argument Against An Army
sharp_disagreements.quote: You encounter further arguments by the pro-Sylvania traitors—again, and again, and a hundred times again—but each time the new argument is handily defeated by 3 to 1.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Always downshifting on each counterargument from a motivated source invites Gish gallop; contradicts filtered-evidence essay.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Downshift is proportional to likelihood ratio; weak galloped arguments move belief negligibly.

sharp_disagreements.title: Rationalization
sharp_disagreements.quote: In Traditional Rationality, there is nothing wrong with the scientist who arrives at a pet hypothesis and then sets out to find an experiment that proves it.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Traditional Rationality (Popper, Reichenbach) demands seeking refutation; prediction-vs-accommodation remains a live dispute.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Practising scientists valued committed advocacy (Mitroff 1974); forward/backward concerns evidence selection, not timing.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Bottom Line
sharp_disagreements.quote: So the handwriting of the curious inquirer is entangled with the signs and portents and the contents of the boxes, whereas the handwriting of the clever arguer is evidence only of which owner paid the higher bid.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Arguer's true facts still inform a knowing listener (Milgrom & Roberts); dismissing by origin is the genetic fallacy.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Next essay handles listener inference; closing paragraph disclaims use as a Fully General Counterargument.

sharp_disagreements.title: Update Yourself Incrementally
sharp_disagreements.quote: Yet it is widely believed, especially in the court of public opinion, that a true theory can have no failures and a false theory no successes.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: No one is cited holding the binary view; Kuhn/Lakatos describe anomaly tolerance; threshold rejection is omitted.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Public binary reasoning observable: snowball, weather-driven belief (Egan & Mullin), p=0.05 dichotomization (McShane & Gal).

sharp_disagreements.title: Update Yourself Incrementally
sharp_disagreements.quote: If the theory is true, supporting evidence will come in shortly, and the probability will climb again.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Supporting evidence arrives at the world's rate, not shortly; cherished beliefs face large, not small, shifts.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Positive KL divergence means evidence drifts toward truth; essay says update now, and 'a little' fits small evidence.

sharp_disagreements.title: What Evidence Filtered Evidence?
sharp_disagreements.quote: But then the clever arguer can make you believe anything they choose, if there is a sufficient variety of signs to selectively report. That doesn’t sound right.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Bayesian persuasion (Kamenica & Gentzkow) shows conditioning on the algorithm bounds but doesn't neutralize manipulation.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Kamenica-Gentzkow receiver is never deceived; Bayes-plausibility is the essay's resolution in theorem form.

sharp_disagreements.title: What Evidence Filtered Evidence?
sharp_disagreements.quote: In a way, no one can really trust the theory of natural selection until after they have listened to creationists for five minutes; and then they know it’s solid.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Exposure to a lone contrarian lowers perceived consensus (Koehler 2016); only inoculation with refutation helps.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Sentence concerns a listener who can evaluate arguments; Koehler concerns authority judgments, not argument quality.

sharp_disagreements.title: Belief in Self-Deception
sharp_disagreements.quote: “So,” I said incredulously, “if God exists or doesn’t exist, that has absolutely no effect on how it would be good for people to think or act? I think even a rabbi would look a little askance at that.”
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Practice over doctrine is mainstream Judaism (Yerushalmi Hagigah, Reconstructionism); a rabbi would recognize it.
sharp_disagreements.gist: She was Orthodox; Maimonides' first principle requires God; the Yerushalmi line continues that practice leads back to God.

sharp_disagreements.title: Belief in Self-Deception
sharp_disagreements.quote: you get the same sort of placebo benefit that would actually come from a successful self-deception
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Religion's benefits flow through congregational friendship, not belief (Lim & Putnam 2010); placebo mechanism unnecessary.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Lim & Putnam support the essay: benefits are social, so her belief-in-self-deception theory is wrong.

sharp_disagreements.title: Belief in Self-Deception
sharp_disagreements.quote: This is why intelligent people only have a certain amount of time (measured in subjective time spent thinking about religion) to become atheists.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: One-conversation generalization; religious switching is common and driven by life events, not a cognitive deadline.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Pew: most switching occurs before 24, a window; the clock measures practiced motivated reasoning.

sharp_disagreements.title: Don’t Believe You’ll Self-Deceive
sharp_disagreements.quote: I realize now that when I wrote “You cannot make yourself believe the sky is green by an act of will,” I wasn’t just a dispassionate reporter of the existing facts. I was also trying to instill a self-fulfilling prophecy.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Instilling a belief for its consequences is belief in belief; affirmations backfire for those who need them.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Tarski forbids false beliefs held for benefit, not true self-fulfilling ones; Wood et al. backfire required implausibility.

sharp_disagreements.title: Don’t Believe You’ll Self-Deceive
sharp_disagreements.quote: Shouldn’t the gut-level realization, “Oh, wait, the sky really isn’t green” follow from the realization “My map that says ‘the sky is green’ has no reason to be correlated with the territory”?
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Meta-knowledge failing to correct belief is the general finding (belief perseverance), undermining the sequence's promise.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Ross, Lepper & Hubbard's process debriefing eliminated perseverance: explaining the mechanism works.

sharp_disagreements.title: Doublethink (Choosing to be Biased)
sharp_disagreements.quote: But we do not have such direct control over our beliefs. You cannot make yourself believe the sky is green by an act of will.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Essay refutes announced self-deception only; indirect, unconscious belief steering is pervasive and functional.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Unconscious steering isn't second-order rationality; positive illusions' benefits contested (Colvin & Block).

sharp_disagreements.title: Doublethink (Choosing to be Biased)
sharp_disagreements.quote: Be irrationally optimistic about your driving skills, and you will be happily unconcerned where others sweat and fear. You won’t have to put up with the inconvenience of a seat belt.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Driver overconfidence is real but no link to seat-belt refusal; optimism bias measurement contested (Shah 2016).
sharp_disagreements.gist: Slovic, Fischhoff & Lichtenstein 1978: belt nonuse stems from per-trip probability neglect; laws came from debiased reasoning.

sharp_disagreements.title: Doublethink (Choosing to be Biased)
sharp_disagreements.quote: Maybe there are stupid happy people out there. Maybe they are happier than you are.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Lower intelligence associates with lower happiness (Ali et al. 2013); 'stupid happy people' undocumented.
sharp_disagreements.gist: The author suspected stupid happiness was overrated; the 'maybe' is a concession for argument's sake.

sharp_disagreements.title: Moore’s Paradox
sharp_disagreements.quote: I don’t think this is correct—relatively young children can understand the concept of having a false belief, which requires separate mental buckets for the map and the territory.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: False-belief tasks concern others; first-person transparency makes the commenter's view closer to standard analysis.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Transparency explains the conflation: sincere Moore sentences mean belief was answered by affect, not the world.

sharp_disagreements.title: Moore’s Paradox
sharp_disagreements.quote: Many people may not consciously distinguish between believing something and endorsing it.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Belief vs acceptance (Cohen, Bratman) is an established legitimate distinction; Kurige's statements reconcilable.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Acceptance is legitimate only when recognized; Kurige's factual claim and the essay's test reveal which attitude is held.

sharp_disagreements.title: No, Really, I’ve Deceived Myself
sharp_disagreements.quote: She hasn’t actually deceived herself into believing that God exists or that the Jewish religion is true. Not even close, so far as I can tell.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Her pattern matches ordinary religious credence (Van Leeuwen 2014); calling it failed self-deception is a stipulation.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Van Leeuwen's credence/belief split makes her self-report of acquired factual belief wrong, as the essay says.

sharp_disagreements.title: Singlethink
sharp_disagreements.quote: More importantly, I realized that I had always known this—that the real memory had always been lurking in a corner of my mind
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Recovered childhood memory and 'always knew' feeling are suspect under reconstructive memory and hindsight.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Hindsight bias runs flattering; this revision was unflattering; the skill of noticing the flinch doesn't depend on the memory.

sharp_disagreements.title: Cached Thoughts
sharp_disagreements.quote: It’s a good guess that the actual majority of human cognition consists of cache lookups.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Hundred-step rule implies parallelism, not caching; fast cognition is pattern completion, not lookup.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay defines cache as pattern completion; Hopfield memory and Logan's instance theory are literal caching.

sharp_disagreements.title: Hold Off On Proposing Solutions
sharp_disagreements.quote: If you’re an evolutionary biologist, anyone you meet can instantly solve any open problem in your field, usually by postulating group selection.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Mocking group selection was dated; multilevel selection had been professionally revived (Wade, Wilson & Wilson 2007).
sharp_disagreements.gist: Laypeople propose naive good-of-species selection; Wilson & Wilson's equivalence means group framing adds nothing.

sharp_disagreements.title: How to Seem (and Be) Deep
sharp_disagreements.quote: You know, given human nature, if people got hit on the head by a baseball bat every week, pretty soon they would invent reasons why getting hit on the head with a baseball bat was a good thing.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Argument is Bostrom & Ord's reversal test, whose evolutionary exceptions may cover death; TMT failed replication.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Senescence isn't tuned for our benefit (Williams 1957); mechanism is effort justification (Aronson & Mills), not TMT.

sharp_disagreements.title: How to Seem (and Be) Deep
sharp_disagreements.quote: But my suspicion is that I came across as “deep” because I coherently violated the cached pattern for “deep wisdom” in a way that made immediate sense.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Perceived profundity depends heavily on the rater (Pennycook 2015); two compliments are weak evidence.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Pennycook's stimuli were vague buzzwords; essay's one-step arguments are evaluable and it hedges its inference.

sharp_disagreements.title: Original Seeing
sharp_disagreements.quote: I don’t know if this story is based on reality or not, but either way, it’s true.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: 'Either way, it's true' is the fictional-evidence move the sequence later condemns.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Story illustrates a testable technique rather than serving as evidence; Fable confirms constrained prompts work.

sharp_disagreements.title: Priming and Contamination
sharp_disagreements.quote: confirmation bias is built directly into our hardware, associational networks priming compatible thoughts and memories
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Spreading activation is symmetric (antonyms prime), so it cannot explain confirmation bias.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Cited experiment shows hypothesis-consistent, not symmetric, activation; positive-test retrieval is confirmation bias.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Genetic Fallacy
sharp_disagreements.quote: They have failed to clear their minds; they could do significantly better by doubting anything the Bible said because the Bible said it.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Doubting the Bible wholesale is itself the genetic fallacy; source reliability is domain-specific.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Establishing domain reliability requires independent evaluation, which is the essay's prescription; biblical ethics mixed.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Logical Fallacy of Generalization from Fictional Evidence
sharp_disagreements.quote: If someone starts out by asking whether or not AIs are gonna put us into capsules like in The Matrix, they’re jumping to a 100-bit proposition, without a corresponding 98 bits of evidence to locate it in the answer space
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Proves too much: the essay's nanotech scenario is equally fictional; stories as hypotheses are legitimate.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay offers widening considerations, not one scenario, and targets stories treated as evidence, not hypotheses.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Virtue of Narrowness
sharp_disagreements.quote: Alas, some unfortunate souls use the same word “evolution” to cover the naturally selected patterns of replicating life, and the strictly accidental structure of stars, and the intelligently configured structure of technology.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Cultural/technological evolution is a mature research program (Boyd & Richerson, Mesoudi et al.), not a category error.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Dual-inheritance theory specifies where the biological analogy breaks, which is the careful usage the essay demands.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Virtue of Narrowness
sharp_disagreements.quote: And don’t even get me started on people who think Wikipedia is an “Artificial Intelligence,” the invention of LSD was a “Singularity,” or that corporations are “superintelligent”!
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Corporations-as-optimizers became a standard alignment analogy; LLMs defy the essay's narrow/general categories.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Bostrom classes organizations as weak collective intelligence, not superintelligent; new phenomena need sharper categories.

sharp_disagreements.title: We Change Our Minds Less Often Than We Think
sharp_disagreements.quote: I realized that once I could guess what my answer would be—once I could assign a higher probability to deciding one way than other—then I had, in all probability, already decided.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Data show underconfidence in self-prediction, not that deliberation had stopped; half-second claim is introspection.
sharp_disagreements.gist: The underconfidence is the title's claim: people think minds are more open than they are.

sharp_disagreements.title: We Change Our Minds Less Often Than We Think
sharp_disagreements.quote: Between hindsight bias, fake causality, positive bias, anchoring/priming, et cetera, et cetera, and above all the dreaded confirmation bias, once an idea gets into your head, it’s probably going to stay there.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Choice blindness and accepted corrections show minds change readily; ideas don't simply stay put.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Johansson et al. 2014: planted, defended choices persist; the title says 'less often', not 'never'.

sharp_disagreements.title: Affective Death Spirals
sharp_disagreements.quote: The phlogiston theory of chemistry could explain just about anything, so long as it didn’t have to predict it in advance.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Phlogiston theory made testable predictions, some failed and some succeeded; it was falsified, not unfalsifiable.
sharp_disagreements.gist: After failed prediction phlogiston was redefined (negative weight); Lavoisier's 'veritable Proteus' matches the essay.

sharp_disagreements.title: Affective Death Spirals
sharp_disagreements.quote: Positive characteristics enhance perception of every other positive characteristic? That sounds a lot like how a fissioning uranium atom sends out neutrons that fission other uranium atoms.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Halo effect is one-shot; no iterative amplification measured; escalation is social group polarization.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Tesser 1978: mere thought polarizes attitudes intrapersonally; group polarization stacks on top.

sharp_disagreements.title: Evaporative Cooling of Group Beliefs
sharp_disagreements.quote: Early studiers of cults were surprised to discover than when cults receive a major shock—a prophecy fails to come true, a moral flaw of the founder is revealed—they often come back stronger than before
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Seekers dissolved, Hardyck & Braden found no increase; Watchtower never officially set 1975 and declined afterward.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Decline, schism and rationalization among remainers is exactly what evaporative cooling predicts; Watchtower admitted 1975 expectations.

sharp_disagreements.title: Every Cause Wants to Be a Cult
sharp_disagreements.quote: It’s a high-entropy state into which the system trends, an attractor in human psychology.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Movements typically routinize and fade, not become cults; the entropy attractor is an unfalsifiable metaphor.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Routinization is a branch of the attractor; essay names a byline test confirmed by Tomkins et al. 2017.

sharp_disagreements.title: Every Cause Wants to Be a Cult
sharp_disagreements.quote: Every group of people with an unusual goal—good, bad, or silly—will trend toward the cult attractor unless they make a constant effort to resist it.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Rationalist community made the prescribed constant effort yet offshoots became cultish; 'constant effort' is underspecified.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Offshoots stopped the effort; the wider community detected and exposed them, as the pump should.

sharp_disagreements.title: Guardians of Ayn Rand
sharp_disagreements.quote: Bayesian probability theory is the quantitative logic of which Aristotle’s qualitative logic is a special case
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Syllogistic is predicate logic; probability theory does not contain it as a special case.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Reading quantifiers as conditional probabilities makes Barbara a probability theorem (Chater & Oaksford 1999).

sharp_disagreements.title: Guardians of Ayn Rand
sharp_disagreements.quote: Actually, I think Shermer’s falling prey to correspondence bias by supposing that there’s any particular correlation between Rand’s philosophy and the way her followers formed a cult.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Rand's sense-of-life doctrine specified the cult mechanism; Shermer had a mechanism, essay substitutes entropy.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Sense-of-life doctrine postdates the cult's formation; essay claims no doctrine immunizes, not that doctrines never matter.

sharp_disagreements.title: Guardians of the Gene Pool
sharp_disagreements.quote: Actually this is a common misconception. Hitler believed that the Aryan superman had previously existed
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Nazi program was forward-looking breeding (Lebensborn, eugenics); calling 'breed supermen' a misconception is wrong.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Nazi racial ends were restorative: degeneration, re-Nordification, aurochs back-breeding; Herf concerns means only.

sharp_disagreements.title: Guardians of the Truth
sharp_disagreements.quote: And yet scientists don’t torture people who question the atomic theory of chemistry. Why not?
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Lysenkoism and eugenics show future-facing science persecuting critics; coercive power, not posture, is the difference.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Lysenkoism replaced experimental criterion with doctrinal authority, as essay predicts; eugenics framed as preventing decline.

sharp_disagreements.title: Guardians of the Truth
sharp_disagreements.quote: Nearly all cultures before the Enlightenment believed in a Fall from Grace—that things had once been perfect in the distant past
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Ideas of progress existed across pre-Enlightenment cultures (Lucretius, Joachim, Nisbet); dichotomy drawn too sharply.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Augustine is Fall-then-restoration, Joachim was condemned; Azoulay et al. show incumbents excluding outsiders.

sharp_disagreements.title: Lonely Dissent
sharp_disagreements.quote: As the case of cryonics testifies, the fear of thinking really different is stronger than the fear of death.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Skydiving vs cryonics is confounded by cost and efficacy; treats factual disagreement as character defect.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Cost is low via insurance; McIntyre & Fahy preservation advance didn't raise sign-ups, so behavior doesn't track evidence.

sharp_disagreements.title: Lonely Dissent
sharp_disagreements.quote: To be a scientific revolutionary, you’ve got to be the first person to contradict what everyone else you know is thinking.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Merton's multiples show the lone first contradictor is mostly a myth; discoveries are usually simultaneous.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Multiples are each alone among their acquaintances; Darwin's 'confessing a murder' shows the personal cost.

sharp_disagreements.title: Mere Messiahs
sharp_disagreements.quote: Relative to most other prophets of his day, he was probably relatively more honest, relatively less violent, and relatively more courageous.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Nothing is known about other prophets' honesty; soul-survival category anachronistic for Second Temple Judaism.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Josephus shows the other prophets were violent; Pharisees held soul imperishable, so afterlife point stands.

sharp_disagreements.title: On Expressing Your Concerns
sharp_disagreements.quote: Together they become more optimistic than either would be on their own, each one’s doubts quelled by the other’s seemingly confident reassurance
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Groups polarize toward initial lean, not always optimism; groupthink model poorly supported.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Persuasive-arguments pooling plus politeness asymmetry yields optimism; Buehler et al. 2005 show group planning optimism.

sharp_disagreements.title: Resist the Happy Death Spiral
sharp_disagreements.quote: The man was Francis Bacon, his Great Idea was the scientific method, and he was the only crackpot in all history to claim that level of benefit to humanity and turn out to be completely right.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Bacon's inductive method wasn't science's method; Ibn al-Haytham preceded him; he discovered nothing.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Essay hedges Bacon's role and credits his prophecy of benefit, which Fable grants was right.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Affect Heuristic
sharp_disagreements.quote: According to ordinary economic theory, return and risk should correlate positively
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Low-volatility anomaly shows risk and return don't correlate positively; essay's correctness standard is a failed model.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Ganzach's familiar/unfamiliar split rules out anomaly-tracking; global evaluation predicts both judgments.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Halo Effect
sharp_disagreements.quote: And—I know you don’t think you have to do it, but maybe you should—be just a little more skeptical of the more attractive political candidates.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Facial competence, not attractiveness, predicts elections (Todorov 2005); advice targets the wrong cue.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Competence-from-face is itself a halo; Berggren et al. 2010 find beauty predicts votes in Finland.

sharp_disagreements.title: The Robbers Cave Experiment
sharp_disagreements.quote: The Robbers Cave Experiment illustrates the psychology of hunter-gatherer bands, echoed through time, as perfectly as any experiment ever devised by social science.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Forager bands have fluid membership and cooperative ties (Hill et al. 2011); ancestral leap is a just-so story.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Intergroup lethality among foragers (Bowles 2009) and chimps coexists with fluid band membership.

sharp_disagreements.title: Unbounded Scales, Huge Jury Awards, and Futurism
sharp_disagreements.quote: It’s not twice as much; more like eight times as much.
sharp_disagreements.fable_gist: Doubling loudness needs about tenfold power, not eightfold; wrong psychophysics number.
sharp_disagreements.gist: Stevens's 0.67 pressure exponent gives eight; ten is the sone convention; both support 'not twice'.

sharp_disagreements.title: Uncritical Supercriticality
sharp_disagreements.quote: New Agers culturally inherit the cached thought that faith is positive, but lack Christianity’s exclusionary scripture to keep out competing memes. New Agers end up in happy death spirals around stars, trees, magnets, diets, spells, unicorns…
